title: Reduction of the ind-etale lift
statement:
For the lift $C=H_A(\overline C)$ of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], the
specified map $C/IC\to\overline C$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $C=H_A(\overline C)$ and $\epsilon:C\to\overline C$ for the cocone map of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Since the structural map $A\to\overline C$ factors through $A/I$, $\epsilon$ kills every product $ac$ with $a\in I$, and hence kills $IC$. Thus it factors uniquely through a ring map $r:R=C/IC\to\overline C$, the specified reduction map. The indexing category is small by its presentation model and filtered by [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered]; its terms are etale of finite presentation, so $C/A$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Tag 097P, lemma-lift-ind-etale, construction of C and induced quotient map

proof.text: Choose a small filtered presentation $\overline C=\varinjlim_i\overline B_i$ by etale finite-presentation $A/I$-algebras, using [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The algebra colimit is also the ring colimit: a compatible family of ring maps has a common restriction from $A/I$ because the filtered category is nonempty and every two indices have a common successor. Give the target ring this common $A/I$-algebra structure; the algebra universal property gives the unique induced ring map, since any ring map extending the cocone respects that structure. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], each $z\in\overline C$ is the image of some $\overline b\in\overline B_i$. By [lem-exc-etale-algebra-lift], choose an etale finite-presentation $A$-algebra $B_i$ and the specified isomorphism $B_i/IB_i\cong\overline B_i$. Choose $b\in B_i$ reducing to $\overline b$. Write $q_i:B_i\to\overline B_i\to\overline C$ for the composite. Finite presentation gives a presentation-model algebra $P_i$ and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $u:P_i\to B_i$. Then $(P_i,q_i\circ u)$ is an object of the indexing category in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. Its structure map sends $u^{-1}(b)$ to an element of $C$ whose image under $\epsilon$ is $q_i(u(u^{-1}(b)))=z$. Hence $\epsilon$, and therefore $r$, is surjective.

source.place: Tag 097P, lemma-lift-ind-etale, third proof paragraph: lift the etale stages and obtain surjectivity

proof.text: The base change of $A\to C$ along $A\to A/I$ is $A/I\to R$: the isomorphism $C\otimes_A(A/I)\cong C/IC$ sends $c\otimes\overline a$ to $ac\bmod IC$, with inverse $c\bmod IC\mapsto c\otimes1$; these are well-defined inverse ring maps by balancing and the quotient relations. Base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes $R$ ind-etale over $A/I$. The target $\overline C$ is ind-etale over $A/I$ by hypothesis, and $r$ is an $A/I$-algebra map. The relative-map clause of that same node makes $r$ ind-etale, hence weakly etale. By the explicit flatness clause in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], $\overline C$ is flat as an $R$-module via $r$.

source.place: Tag 097P, lemma-lift-ind-etale, third proof paragraph: permanence and flatness

proof.text: Put $J=\ker r$. Surjectivity gives an $R$-linear ring isomorphism $R/J\to\overline C$, $[a]\mapsto r(a)$: its inverse sends $z$ to the class of any preimage, independently of the choice since two preimages differ by $J$. Thus $R/J$ is flat over $R$: for any injection of $R$-modules, tensoring this isomorphism identifies the induced tensor map with that for the flat module $\overline C$. Apply [lem-exc-flat-quotient-element-equation] to obtain, for each $x\in J$, an $e\in J$ with $x=xe$.

source.place: Tag 097P, lemma-lift-ind-etale, third proof paragraph; Algebra Tag 04PS, implication (1) => (5)

proof.text: For such $e$, choose $\widetilde e\in C$ with image $e$ in $R=C/IC$. Since $e\in\ker r$, $\epsilon(\widetilde e)=0$ and $\epsilon(1-\widetilde e)=1$. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-units], $1-\widetilde e$ is invertible in $C$. Reducing its inverse modulo $IC$ shows that $1-e$ is invertible in $R$. But $x=xe$ implies $x(1-e)=0$; multiplication by that inverse gives $x=0$. Thus $\ker r=0$. Together with surjectivity this proves that the specified map $r$ is an isomorphism.
